## Natural history notes

A small crambid moth characterized by its satiny pale yellow to whitish wings, delicate body, and subtle brown or golden markings that can give the wings a glossy appearance. In Florida, it is found in grassy areas, wetlands, marsh edges, roadsides, fields, and other open habitats where grasses and sedges are common. Adults are usually active at night and may come to lights, while the caterpillars likely feed on grasses or related herbaceous plants, helping connect low vegetation with nocturnal moth and insect food webs.
